items.action: Patch to 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28 (or FIPS 14.1-73.41 FIPS / 13.1-37.282) immediately; apply Citrix Global Deny Lists as interim mitigation and hunt for repeated appliance crashes.
items.details: Unauthenticated attackers can crash the nsaaad authentication service with crafted SAML requests, knocking VPN/SSO offline. Affects 14.1 before 14.1-73.41 and 13.1 before 13.1-64.28 on appliances configured as SAML SP or IdP. Prior patches for CVE-2026-88771/88772 do NOT cover it — organizations that patched last week must upgrade again. Researchers are investigating possible RCE beyond DoS.
items.summary: CVE-2026-88779, a memory-overflow flaw in NetScaler ADC/Gateway SAML authentication, is being actively exploited as a zero-day; CISA added it to the KEV catalog on Oct 4 with a federal patch deadline of October 7.
items.title: Citrix NetScaler SAML zero-day under active attack — CISA deadline today

items.action: Upgrade to fixed versions in a change window; if patching is delayed, restrict internet-facing access to the instances immediately.
items.details: Atlassian sent customers an 'Action required' email on Oct 6. Exploitation requires knowing the exact filename and path, and directory listings are not possible — but sensitive files in some configurations raise the risk. Fixed versions are available now.
items.summary: CVE-2026-21589 (CVSS 9.3) lets an unauthenticated attacker read specific files within the web application root of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Software, Jira Service Management, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible and Fisheye Data Center.
items.title: Atlassian warns of critical file-access flaw in datacenter products

items.action: Install the out-of-band cumulative updates (KB5129955–KB5129958) on all on-prem Exchange servers; confirm Exchange 2016/2019 ESU enrollment.
items.details: Released Oct 2, ahead of Patch Tuesday. Exchange Online received a service-side fix (cloud customers need no action). Affected: Exchange Subscription Edition RTM, 2019 CU14/CU15, 2016 CU23 — the 2016/2019 builds need ESU Period 2 enrollment (expiring October 2026) to receive the patch. Discovered by Microsoft researcher Jan Mitchell.
items.summary: CVE-2026-96940 (CVSS 8.8): weak authorization in on-premises Exchange Server lets an authenticated attacker read other users' mailboxes — messages and attachments — within the same organization. Microsoft rates exploitation 'More Likely'.
items.title: Microsoft ships out-of-band Exchange fix for mailbox-read escalation

items.action: Treat listings as indicators of compromise; hunt for Everest tooling and watch for leaked-sample drops before concluding scope.
items.details: Everest has also hit Dutch firm B-accountants. As with most leak-site claims, a listing is not proof of compromise: no victim has acknowledged an incident and no data has been independently verified.
items.summary: ThreatMon dark-web monitoring reported Everest ransomware listings for industrial manufacturer Kennametal and Dubai airline flydubai on Oct 6 — claims that remain unconfirmed by either organization.
items.title: Everest claims Kennametal and flydubai in fresh victim listings

items.action: Watch for an HHS breach filing, a leak-site claim, or a UIC statement naming affected individuals; reset UIC-linked credentials as a precaution.
items.details: The responsible group, ransom demand, and scope — including whether protected health information is involved — are unconfirmed. If PHI is in scope, HIPAA breach notification to HHS follows within 60 days.
items.summary: Ransomware struck the University of Illinois Chicago College of Medicine with confirmed data exfiltration; UIC has acknowledged the incident.
items.title: Ransomware hits UIC College of Medicine, data stolen

items.action: Monitor for sample-data drops on the LockBit leak site and any revised statement from the bank.
items.details: The incident report is based on BreachSense leak monitoring; the bank's customer notice acknowledges service disruption only. Scope of any data theft is unknown.
items.summary: LockBit 3.0 listed capitalbankhaiti.biz as a victim on Oct 5; the bank posted a notice Oct 4 about server-access issues, stating customer data is not affected. Neither claim is independently confirmed.
items.title: LockBit 3.0 claims Capital Bank Haiti; bank cites 'technical incident'

items.action: Do not treat listings as breach confirmations; corroborate with network telemetry and leak-site evidence before alerting stakeholders.
items.details: No independent evidence of data theft or encryption has surfaced for either; neither company has issued a statement.
items.summary: ThreatMon reported Akira listing Hygrade and Qilin listing Corby Rock Mill on Oct 6 — threat-intel leads, not confirmed breaches or confirmed encryption events.
items.title: Akira and Qilin add Hygrade and Corby Rock Mill to victim lists

items.action: Policy and IR teams: track the Oct 17 order — it sets precedent on who investigates insurer breaches; Star Health customers should watch for official breach notices.
items.details: MeitY told the court IRDA, not the Centre, should investigate. The petition also seeks halting Star Health's online operations and a probe into claims that the CISO sold customer data to a hacker ('xenZen').
items.summary: A petition by cybersecurity researcher Himanshu Pathak before the Madras High Court seeks a probe into the alleged Star Health breach said to expose personal data of ~3.1 crore customers; Justice Dhandapani will rule on Oct 17 whether the Union government can order the inquiry.
items.title: Madras HC petition seeks probe into Star Health data breach

items.action: Customers: monitor for phishing referencing Teleforce services; validate dataset attribution (record formats, timestamps) before treating this as a confirmed breach.
items.details: Threat level assessed as medium-unverified: claims could be recycled or misattributed datasets. Watch for phishing leveraging any leaked contact/telephone data.
items.summary: An Oct 6 dark-web intelligence post references an alleged data exposure tied to Indian cloud-telephony provider Teleforce; the company has not confirmed any breach and no dataset size or attacker is established.
items.title: Alleged Teleforce Cloud Telephony data surfaces on the dark web

items.action: Patch SharePoint urgently; threat-hunt for prior Warlock footholds rather than relying on current version checks.
items.details: Symantec tied the same actor to active SharePoint exploitation earlier this week. Lesson for Indian government, BFSI and infra orgs: internet-facing SharePoint must be inventoried, patched and hunted for historical compromise.
items.summary: Researchers report the Warlock/Longlegs/Storm-2603 cluster continues exploiting Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities — including against Indian targets — to disable security controls and deploy ransomware, hitting a water utility, telecom provider, government body and university.
items.title: China-linked Warlock keeps hammering SharePoint at critical infrastructure
